{{Quote|We don't do weddings.|Figrin D'an|<ref name="We Don't Do Weddings: The Band's Tale">{{StoryCite|story=We Don't Do Weddings: The Band's Tale|book=Tales from the Mos Eisley Cantina}}</ref>}}
'''"Fiery" Figrin D'an''' (alias '''Barbarine''') was a [[Gender/Legends|male]] [[Bith/Legends|Bith]] who was the leader of the [[Band/Legends|band]] the [[Figrin D'an and the Modal Nodes/Legends|Modal Nodes]] and the younger brother of [[Barquin D'an/Legends|Barquin D'an]]. Specializing in [[Jizz/Legends|Jizz]] [[Music/Legends|music]], Figrin played a reed instrument known as a [[Kloo horn/Legends|Kloo horn]], as well as a percussion instrument called a [[Gasan string drum/Legends|Gasan string drum]]. Like his band mates, Figrin was registered with the [[Intergalactic Federation of Musicians]] (IFM). Regions of Figrin's highly evolved [[Brain/Legends|brain]] allowed him a special acuity when it came to analyzing and relating to music. In fact, the [[Devaronian/Legends|Devaronian]] music fan [[Kardue'sai'Malloc/Legends|Labria]] called him possibly the greatest klooist in [[The galaxy/Legends|the galaxy]]. As such, his talents helped to greatly enhance the quality and popularity of the Modal Nodes' music.

==Biography==
{{Quote|Figrin plays the kloo like a Jedi Master, but as a band leader he's just short of the dark side.|Doikk Na'ts|<ref name="We Don't Do Weddings: The Band's Tale audio">[[We Don't Do Weddings: The Band's Tale (audio drama)|"We Don't Do Weddings: The Band's Tale" audio drama]]</ref>}}
[[File:Figrin-dan.jpg|thumb|left|Figrin D'an performing in [[Chalmun's Spaceport Cantina/Legends|Chalmun's Spaceport Cantina.]]]]

Shortly before the [[Battle of Yavin/Legends|Battle of Yavin]], Figrin D'an and the Modal Nodes had entered into an exclusive contract with the [[Tatooine/Legends|Tatooine]] [[Crime lord/Legends|crime lord]], [[Jabba Desilijic Tiure/Legends|Jabba Desilijic Tiure]]. They would routinely perform in the courts at [[Jabba's Palace/Legends|Jabba's Palace]] and his [[Mos Eisley/Legends|Mos Eisley]] [[Desilijic Complex/Legends|townhouse]], but it didn't take long before they all regretted entering into a contract with the Hutt. Recognizing Jabba's penchant for executing underlings that displeased him at a moment's notice, the Modal Nodes began to fear for their lives. It would only be a matter of time before Jabba decided to make a snack of the musicians, by tossing one down into the dungeon abode of his pet [[Rancor/Legends|rancor]]. Fortunately for them, a golden opportunity was fresh at hand.

One of Jabba's rivals, a [[Whiphid/Legends|Whiphid]] named [[Lady/Legends|Lady]] [[Valarian/Legends|Valarian]], offered the band 3,000 [[Galactic Credit Standard/Legends|credits]] to perform at her [[Wedding of Valarian and D'Wopp|wedding]] to the Whiphid hunter, [[D'Wopp]]. Figrin decided that the fast money would enable them to get off Tatooine and out from under the thumb of Jabba the Hutt. They arrived at the [[Star Chamber Café]] reception hall inside of the [[Lucky Despot]] Hotel & Casino in Mos Eisley. During one of their set breaks, Figrin took the band's retainer and spent the bulk of it at the casino's [[Sabacc/Legends|sabacc]] tables. The other musicians grew gravely concerned. Thanks to Figrin's gambling, their chances of getting off Tatooine alive were quickly dwindling.

Jabba learned of the Modal Nodes breach of contract and sent several of his [[Bounty hunter/Legends|bounty hunters]] down to the casino to disrupt the festivities. As luck would have it, Imperial [[Stormtrooper/Legends|stormtroopers]] likewise raided the party and a massive fire-fight broke out. During the confusion, the Modal Nodes met a party guest named [[Wuher/Legends|Wuher]] who showed them a quick way out. Wuher put in a good word for them with [[Chalmun/Legends|Chalmun]]&mdash;a [[Wookiee/Legends|Wookiee]] who owned a nearby [[Chalmun's Spaceport Cantina/Legends|cantina]] where Wuher tended bar. Chalmun hired the Modal Nodes to play a couple of gigs at his bar, the following evening. They were performing the night when [[Luke Skywalker/Legends|Luke Skywalker]] and [[Obi-Wan Kenobi/Legends|Obi-Wan Kenobi]] entered the cantina seeking a pilot willing to ferry them to the [[Alderaan/Legends|Alderaan]] system. They continued to perform at Chalmun's on a regular basis. Occasionally, Chalmun's nightshift manager, [[Ackmena/Legends|Ackmena]], would liven the bar's atmosphere by singing along with the Modal Nodes' rhythms.

Shortly after this event, Figrin D'an wagered the band's instruments and equipment on a hand of Sabacc. He lost the bet to [[Kardue'sai'Malloc/Legends|Labria]], but the Modal Nodes soon convinced him to win their equipment back. He eventually succeeded and the Modal Nodes went on to play the intergalactic circuit.

==Personality and traits==
Like many Bith, Figrin D'an had no allegiance when it came to those in positions of power and he considered himself politically neutral. This aided him in protecting the group from any hazardous [[Galactic Empire/Legends|Imperial]] influences.

As a band-leader, "Fiery" Figrin D'an was extremely demanding. He was highly critical of every performance and criticized the band heavily if they were to miss even a single note. With the exception of [[Dorenian Beshniquel/Legends|Fizzz]]-player [[Doikk Na'ts/Legends|Doikk Na'ts]], Figrin owned all of the band-members instruments and equipment. Figrin was never shy when it came to doling out orders to the others.

Aside from being a perfectionist, Figrin was also a [[Glitterstim/Legends|glitterstim]] addict, and a compulsive gambler. He was always open towards accepting contracts if he knew that a Sabacc table and some spice would be close at hand.

==Behind the scenes==
[[File:FigrinDanEGC.jpg|thumb|160px|Figrin D'an.]]

His name is also spelled as '''Figrin Da'n''' in ''Tales from the Mos Eisley Cantina''.

Although many sources claim makeup artist [[Rick Baker]] portrayed Figrin D'an, [[Tom Spina]] confirmed in an email, that the actual portrayer of Figrin D'an was [[Phil Tippett]].<ref name="Tom Spina Email">{{EmailCite|email=File:ModalNodesActorsConfirmation.png|creator=[[Tom Spina]]|date=2021-08-31}}</ref>

In the ''[[Ultimate Alien Anthology]]'', "Figrin Da'n" appears as an example name. This is likely a misspelling of Figrin D'an.
